newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Three killed in fighting in Somali port city.
newsitem.headline: Three killed in fighting in Somali port city.

text.p: At least three people were killed in fighting in the Somali port of Kismayo between Islamic militiamen and gunmen loyal to a local faction leader, witnesses said on Thursday.
They said by radio from Kismayo Islamic militiamen seized Kismayo port on Wednesday and fighters loyal to General Omar Haji Hersi "Morgan" then attacked in vain in a bid to recapture it.
Ali Jama, a former port manager, said at least three people were killed and 15 were wounded in the heavy fighting despite the intervention of clan elders who tried to end the dispute.
The Islamic militiamen are drawn from the same sub-clan as the forces of Morgan, a son-in-law of late former dictator Mohamed Siad Barre who was overthrown at the start of civil war in 1991.

Morgan's forces have held Kismayu, considered the Indian Ocean gateway to the breadbasket of southern Somalia, since expelling in 1993 militiamen loyal to south Mogadishu-based faction leader Mohamed Farah Aideed, who died on August 1.
